codeReview.summary: Clean, minimal implementation that correctly wires FIRMWARE_VERSION to all three MQTT surfaces (state JSON, HA discovery, diagnostics). The feature leverages existing test coverage in launa-mqtt rather than adding redundant tests in the app crate, which is appropriate since app/ cannot run unit tests on native.

issues.description: The publish_discovery() method hand-rolls the device_info JSON string with embedded sw_version using format!(), while launa-mqtt's DiscoveryBuilder already handles sw_version via serde_json. This is a pre-existing pattern (not introduced by this commit), but the hand-rolled JSON is fragile — if FIRMWARE_VERSION contained unescaped quotes, the JSON would break. The existing launa-mqtt tests cover this for status_to_json via escape_json_string(), but the hand-rolled discovery configs in mqtt_client.rs have no such escaping. This is low-risk since CARGO_PKG_VERSION comes from Cargo.toml (a controlled source), but worth noting for future refactoring to use DiscoveryBuilder.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The app/src/mqtt_client.rs publish_discovery() hand-rolls JSON device_info strings instead of using launa-mqtt's DiscoveryBuilder. This architectural pattern (duplicate hand-rolled discovery vs. using the library's builder) is documented in architecture.md as 'MqttClient uses DiscoveryBuilder from launa-mqtt for HA auto-discovery', which is inaccurate — publish_discovery() does NOT use DiscoveryBuilder, it hand-rolls all discovery config JSON strings inline.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: app/src/mqtt_client.rs:600-640 hand-rolls all discovery configs with format!() strings; crates/launa-mqtt/src/discovery.rs has DiscoveryBuilder that does the same thing properly. architecture.md line 'MqttClient uses DiscoveryBuilder from launa-mqtt for HA auto-discovery' is misleading.

VAL-CORE-030.evidence: app/src/main.rs:71 defines `const FIRMWARE_VERSION: &str = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION");` which is evaluated at compile time and embedded in the binary. Cargo.toml version is 0.1.0.

VAL-CORE-031.description: Firmware version included in MQTT state JSON
VAL-CORE-031.evidence: app/src/mqtt_client.rs:574 passes `Some(crate::FIRMWARE_VERSION)` to `status_to_json()` as the firmware_version parameter. launa-mqtt state.rs:91-93 correctly formats this as a quoted JSON string. Test `test_status_to_json_with_firmware_version` verifies this.

VAL-CORE-032.description: Firmware version included in HA discovery config
VAL-CORE-032.evidence: app/src/mqtt_client.rs:617-618 includes `"sw_version":"{}"` in the device_info format string, populated with `crate::FIRMWARE_VERSION`. This sw_version appears in every HA discovery config payload via the device_info variable.

VAL-CORE-033.description: Firmware version included in diagnostics payload
VAL-CORE-033.evidence: app/src/main.rs:389 adds `"fw_version":"{}"` to the diagnostics JSON format string, populated with FIRMWARE_VERSION constant at line 398.

VAL-CORE-034.description: Firmware version null-safe in state JSON
VAL-CORE-034.evidence: launa-mqtt state.rs:91-93 handles `None` by producing the JSON literal `null` (unquoted), and `Some(v)` by producing a properly escaped quoted string. Test `test_status_to_json_all_fields` verifies firmware_version is null when None is passed. Test `test_escape_json_string_firmware_with_special_chars` verifies proper escaping.

summary: The add-firmware-versioning feature is correctly implemented. The FIRMWARE_VERSION const is properly defined using env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION") in app/src/main.rs and wired to all three required surfaces: MQTT state JSON (via status_to_json), HA auto-discovery configs (via sw_version in device_info), and diagnostics payload (via fw_version field). Existing test coverage in launa-mqtt adequately covers the null-safety and string-escaping requirements. One non-blocking concern: the hand-rolled JSON in publish_discovery() doesn't escape the version string (unlike status_to_json which uses escape_json_string), but this is low-risk since CARGO_PKG_VERSION is a controlled value from Cargo.toml. The worker followed the rust-app-worker skill procedure correctly, ran all required verification commands, and the feature passes all 5 validation assertions.
